Quid hoc ad tempus Reformationis, quo non novum Evangelium proferendum, sed vetus jam olim prædicatum & plantatum, Christi & Apostolorum miraculis corroboratum, at hominum flagitio obscuratum, manentibus interim testibus & officio suo strenuè defungentibus, jure postliminij plenissimam in lucem vindicandum fuerat? Si igitur Evangelium idem á nobis prædicari probaverimus, illius temporis miracula nostra utique erunt. In doctrinæ igitur & Evangelij jam olim prædicati consensu totius negotij cardo volvitur. Novimus adventum Antichristi fore in signis & miraculis mendacij. At eos, qui se Antichristo opponent, miracula edituros, nusquam legimus. A deo ut si miracula jactaremus, gravissimo adversus nos præjudicio locū cessuri simus.
units.tr: Clearly he means the kind of darkness that leaves no room for the light or the Gospel already preached before. For he is speaking of the miracles performed at the time of John the Baptist. But at that time the Gospel had neither been preached nor planted, and a new state of the Church had to be introduced; so miracles were needed. What has this to do with the time of the Reformation, when the Gospel was not to be brought forward as something new, but the old Gospel, long since preached and planted, and confirmed by the miracles of Christ and the Apostles, though obscured by men's wickedness, was to be vindicated in full light by right of postliminy, while the witnesses remained and faithfully performed their office? If therefore we prove that the same Gospel is preached by us, our miracles will certainly be of that same kind. The whole matter thus turns on the agreement of doctrine with the Gospel long since preached. We know that the coming of Antichrist will be in lying signs and miracles. But we nowhere read that those who oppose Antichrist will perform miracles. If we boasted of miracles, we would give our opponents a very serious advantage against us.

units.la: XXIX. Quæ porro de tenebris circa tempus Reformationis, & de Ecclesia, quæ juxta Breitingeri sententiam tunc periit, adeoque miraculorum, ipso Melanchthone judice, necessitate disputas, aniles nugæ sunt. Equidem tenebras tantum non Cimmerias & Ægyptiacas Reformationem præcessisse, certum est. Id ex consessione ipsorum Papistarum demonstratum á nostris. At perijsse tunc Ecclesiam, Breitingerus, cui hoc falso imputat Sophista, non dixit. Verba ejus sunt: Die Zeit so diß Weib (Ecclesiam intelligit ex Apoc. XVIII.) in der Wüste seyn sol/ist eben die Zeit/ in deren die liebe Kirchen sich von den Leuthen müssen verlieren/unbekant seyn und verborgen liegen/und doch verbleiben in ihrem wesen. Quod existit, & essentiam permanentem habet, amitti equidem & abscondi, at perire dici non potest. Nunquam Ecclesia vera periit. Nunquam ei inferorum prævaluerunt portæ. At amitti quandoque ex conspectu hominum, illustrem esse, ut ipsi loquuntur, instar Lutetiæ, Madriti, Gandavi illustrissimarum urbium, esse non debuisse, id vero prophetiæ clarissimæ præsagierunt.
units.tr: XXIX. As for what you argue about darkness around the time of the Reformation, and about the Church, which according to Breitinger's view then perished, and therefore about the necessity of miracles, by Melanchthon's own judgment, these are old wives' tales. It is certain indeed that the Reformation was preceded by darkness hardly less than Cimmerian or Egyptian, as our people have shown from the very confession of the Papists themselves. But Breitinger, to whom the Sophist falsely imputes this, did not say that the Church then perished. His words are: "The time in which this woman (he means the Church, from Revelation 18) is to be in the wilderness is precisely the time in which the dear Church must lose herself from the people, be unknown and lie hidden, and yet remain in her being." What exists and has a lasting essence may indeed be lost and hidden, but it cannot be said to perish. The true Church has never perished; the gates of hell have never prevailed against her. But that she is sometimes removed from the sight of men, and was not supposed to be as famous as the most illustrious cities, as they themselves put it, like Paris, Madrid, or Ghent, this the clearest prophecy had foretold.

units.la: XXX. Hæc attulisse impræsentiarum sufficiat. Arduum non erit pio lectori ἐκ τῆς κρυπτῆς γινώσκειν τὸ ὕψασμα. Cæterum quæ pro Diva sua Eremitana, hoc est, pro aris & focis suis magno conatu nugas majores agitans dixit, quàm vana sint omnia, & sophismatum plena, proximè ut cognoscat, dabimus ξὺν Θεῷ καὶ πόνῳ operam. Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ!
units.tr: XXX. It will be enough to have brought forward these points for now. It will not be hard for the pious reader to know the sublime from what is hidden [ἐκ τῆς κρυπτῆς γινώσκειν τὸ ὕψασμα]. Otherwise, we will with God's help and labour [ξὺν Θεῷ καὶ πόνῳ] take care to show how empty and full of sophisms all the greater trifles are that he has put forward with great effort on behalf of his divine Eremite, that is, for their altars and hearths. Glory to God in the highest! [Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ!]

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: An Ecclesiam ante Reformationem perisse fateatur Breitingerus?
units.tr: Does Breitinger admit that the Church perished before the Reformation?
